meta: Midnight, your "son" calls asking for $800 right away, and the voice sounds exactly right. But it could be a voice clone: AI copying a voice from a short recording taken from a video you posted.

muc.title: A call in the middle of the night
muc.text: Midnight, the phone rings. Her son's voice: Mom, I'm in trouble, send me $800 right now. The voice sounds exactly the same, but the caller isn't her son.

muc.title: Copying a voice from a short recording
muc.text: That's a voice clone: AI copying a voice. Scammers only need a short recording, taken from a video you posted online, to copy a voice.

muc.title: Three signs
muc.text: Watch for three signs: they rush you, they ask you to send money or read out a one-time code (OTP), and they tell you not to tell anyone.

muc.title: Hang up and call back yourself
muc.text: The surest way: hang up, then call back yourself on the number you already have saved. Don't call back the number that just called.

muc.title: Something only family knows
muc.text: Or ask something only family would know, like what everyone had for dinner yesterday. A scammer can't answer.

muc.title: Share less of your voice
muc.text: Prevent it ahead of time: post fewer public videos with voices, especially of older family members and young kids.

muc.title: Send this to your parents
muc.text: Send this video to your parents, and agree on a rule: for urgent money matters, always call back to check.
